notes: 2 Connecticut ZIPs have a land-area difference over 0.5% between the 2020 county file and the 2022 town file; the town file is used.
ZIP parts in the excluded uninhabited island areas were dropped: 96799->60040.
33791 ZIPs (ZCTAs); 10069 span more than one county; 4602 have no county holding 80% or more of their land (the engine asks the user to choose).

County map: 3222 features from the 1:20,000,000 file, coordinates rounded to 3 decimals, RFC 7946 winding (exterior counter-clockwise); 0.299 MB gzipped. Not on the map (not in the 1:20m file): 60010, 60020, 60050, 66010, 69100, 69110, 69120, 78010, 78020, 78030.

Canonical county list: the 2024 1:500,000 cartographic county file (3232 counties and equivalents, including Connecticut's 9 planning regions and Puerto Rico), minus 60030 (Rose Island, American Samoa (uninhabited atoll)), 60040 (Swains Island, American Samoa (no NRI record)), 69085 (Northern Islands, Northern Mariana Islands (no NRI record)).
Internal points come from the 2024 Gazetteer; for 10 island-area counties not in the Gazetteer (60010, 60020, 60050, 66010, 69100, 69110, 69120, 78010, 78020, 78030) the polygon centroid is used.
NCA5 region per state: the region polygon holding most of the state's county internal points; islands outside the generalised polygons use their chapter region (AS, GU, MP, VI).

Connecticut: ZIP shares for Connecticut come from the 2022 town-to-ZCTA file, so they point at planning regions (091xx). ct_crosswalk.csv records the land-area overlap of the 8 retired counties and 9 regions, used to convert sources that still report old counties.

states.csv: `coastal` means a marine (ocean, gulf or tidal estuary) shoreline; Pennsylvania counts through the tidal Delaware estuary. `great_lakes` means a Great Lakes shoreline. These two flags are curated, not downloaded.

sources.name: NRI item metadata and Terms & Conditions

notes: Fields that NRI v1.20 does not publish (left empty): DRGT_EXPB, DRGT_EXPP, DRGT_EALB, DRGT_EALP, DRGT_HLRB, DRGT_ALRB. Drought is modelled for agriculture only.

3232 counties, 45853 hazard rows. Kept per hazard: AFREQ, EXPB, EXPP, EALB, EALP, EALT, HLRB, ALRB, RISKS; per county: POPULATION, BUILDVALUE, EAL_VALT, SOVI_SCORE, RESL_SCORE, CRF_VALUE. Values rounded to 4 significant figures. Hazard rows where every field is empty (hazard not applicable) are omitted.
536 counties are coastal and 118 have a tsunami zone by the definitions above (derived by Ready Reckoner, not FEMA fields).

Terms compliance: only the trimmed, rounded county fields the model uses are shipped (never the raw table); the About screen and the packet show the citation and disclaimer; numbers Ready Reckoner derives from NRI are labelled as ours.

definitions.coastal: A county is coastal when NRI v1.20 assigns it coastal-flooding building exposure (CFLD_EXPB > 0).

The Federal Government or FEMA cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from the Agency's website(s).
definitions.tsunami_zone: A county has a tsunami zone when NRI v1.20 assigns it tsunami building or population exposure (TSUN_EXPB > 0 or TSUN_EXPP > 0).
